messages:
anya: quick one — our judge ensemble CI is blowing up on tie-heavy eval sets after the quantized bring-up. thinking we should run a synthetic-annotator holdout to calibrate tie thresholds before gating. anyone seen similar?

sam: seen noise from quantized judges before. can you paste failing log and the exact CI job?

anya: failing job is `ci/evals/judge-calibrate` (recent run 2025-02-14). repro steps: 1) run eval-runner on holdout prompts 2) score with ensemble (3 judges) 3) count ties where top scores within 0.01. getting ~18% ties on short-answer set.

liam: that's high. are you comparing float -> q4/8 variants? quantization can shrink scoring head variance. we had similar with the 2B judge.

anya: yes, float vs q4_0. float ties ~3%, q4 ties ~17%. weirdly deterministic tie pairs differ (ordering flips).

maria: proposal: use synthetic annotators derived from prompt templates + label noise to estimate tie probability and calibrate a tie-breaking margin per-model. then bake that margin into CI gating (fail if post-margin accuracy drop > 1.5%).

harper: flagged: we need fairness sweep across demographics before we auto-apply lexical tie-breakers. small-g model tie-breaker could bias certain phrasing. add stratified slices (gender, dialect, domain).

sam: agree. practical plan: 1) build synthetic annotator generator (template + perturbations) 2) run stratified holdout (N=2k per slice) 3) compute tie-rate and per-slice delta when applying candidate tie-breaker 4) if any slice delta > 2%, block.

anya: I sketched generator prompts: `You are an annotator. Given the question and candidate responses, pick best. Annotator personality: concise/lenient/noisy.` use temperature variety to simulate annotator disagreement.

ci-bot: ci/evals/judge-calibrate #452 failed — tests: tie-rate-threshold, adjudicator-consistency. See: https://ci.redwood.dev/ci/452 (logs attached)

anya: attaching short log snippet: ```
[2025-02-14T17:03:12Z] eval-runner: scored 2000 examples
[2025-02-14T17:03:12Z] ensemble: ties_detected=360 (18.0%)
[2025-02-14T17:03:12Z] adjudicator: q4_0 vs float agreement=0.84
[2025-02-14T17:03:12Z] runner ERROR: kv-cache OOM on device:0 — retried 2x
```

liam: runner ERROR might explain some nondeterminism — tracker is ENG-RUNNER-337. kv-cache OOM causes partial re-evals and different softmax tails. patch incoming that stabilizes caching order.

maria: small pragmatic tie-breaker we used elsewhere: lexical-score = lexical_similarity(candidate, prompt) * 0.001. Apply only when abs(score_diff) < margin. That kept bias small in prior tests but still need slices.

harper: we should evaluate lexical tie-breaker on synthetic annotators plus a human-annotated fairness holdout (200 examples). I'll volunteer to run the human pass.

sam: can we add a CI canary to try proposed pipeline: `ci/evals/judge-calibrate-canary` run nightly for a week, using q4 judges and synthetic annotators + fairness holdout? if passes, promote to gate.

anya: yes. I'll open PR with: 1) synthetic annotator harness, 2) per-model margin calc, 3) canary job defs, 4) docs. pinging @liam for runner patch dependency. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/evals/pull/987 (WIP).

liam: I'll push runner fix to that branch today. quick ask: can we lower the tie margin computation to use median absolute diff rather than mean? more robust to outliers.

maria: +1 to median. Also log the tie pair tokens so we can inspect semantic vs lexical ties (helps bias review).

anya: assigned tasks: anya -> PR and canary def, liam -> runner patch and reproducible CI image, harper -> human fairness pass, sam -> automation for per-slice gating. set milestone: `judge-calibrate-EPIC` target next Tue.

harper: :thumbsup: will start human pass tomorrow.

sam: I'll stub the canary job in CI and add alerts if any slice delta > 1%.

ci-bot: note: job quota for nightly canaries is limited; coordinate with eng-infra before enabling.

anya: thanks all. will update PR and add sample synthetic prompts in the repo. ping if you want a local repro image. :sparkles:

sam: thanks — moving to tracking ticket ENG-EVAL-221.
